text: {"domains":{"block_M":[64,128],"block_N":[64,128,256],"block_K":[32,64],"num_stages":[1,2,3,4],"threads":[128],"swizzle":[0,4,8,16,32,64]},"shared_memory_limit":32768,"weights":{"traffic":1,"launches":1,"pipeline":1,"footprint":1},"rationale":"Two failures (attempt-01 863.78us, attempt-02 679.45us) both selected block_M=32 with block_N=256 and swizzle=64; the baseline 128x64x64,s1,t128,sw0 remains best at 470.78us. Simulated DRAM stayed 16.78MB in all runs, so swizzle-driven panel reuse is not reflected in simulator traffic; analytic reuse hypothesis unsupported. Dropping block_M=32 to stop HiGHS re-picking the wide-N small-M corner, and keeping block_N=256 exploratory but hoping larger block_M wins. Reverting threads to [128] since 256 correlated with the worst result, isolating tile/stage/swizzle effects. Kept block_K [32,64], num_stages up to 4, and full swizzle set so HiGHS can still test stages=4 and moderate swizzle with wide-M tiles. Uniform weights retained because traffic proxy has not tracked latency; footprint may still matter through smem feasibility only. Next hypothesis: larger block_M (128) with moderate block_N and stages=2-3, threads=128, beats 470.78us. Validation scope: Metal executes exact source/config/TIR; GB10 numbers are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality claimed."}
